diabolica.name: Maschera Diabolica
diabolica.text: A mask resembling the depths of hell and their vicious guardians.

fiabesco.name: Maschera Fiabesco
fiabesco.text: A mask that makes those beholding you feel as though they stand in an enchanted forest, speaking to the Fairy Queen herself.

angelico.name: Maschera Angelico
angelico.text: A mask resembling the fields of Elysium, green gardens above and silk-like wings of the angels depicted in the most beautiful canvases.

umano.name: Maschera Umano
umano.text: A mask that resembles the creature with the most potential: a humanoid.

features.name: College of the Masquerade
features.text: "You have never been yourself," a voice in your head speaks. "You always wore a mask, always hidden in the crowd, in plain sight." The voice speaks the truth: a mask has always been your identity, your strong side and your greatest weakness. Perhaps you were raised on the stage, among the festivals, always moving in line with a great group of actors and singers, or you were raised in politics as a diplomat, and it took it out of you. You always had to hide your face. No matter how charming it was, you needed a mask to hide who you are or some of your features. Nevertheless, the mask is who you are and an actual part of you.

features.name: The Masquerade
features.text: When you reach 3rd level, the nature of your inspirational magic fuses with your masks. Choose two of the following: Maschera Diabolica, Maschera Angelico, Maschera Fiabesco, or Maschera Umano. Donning a Mask. As a Bonus Action, you can don one of your masks. While wearing a mask, you can take the form of a creature of its type. The mask lasts for 10 minutes, until you are incapacitated, or until you remove it (no action required). You can only wear one mask at a time; donning a new mask ends the previous one. You can don a mask a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. If you have no uses remaining, you can expend a Bardic Inspiration die to don a mask instead. Masked Resilience. While wearing a mask, you gain temporary hit points equal to your Charisma modifier + your bard level. These temporary hit points vanish when the mask is removed. Assume Form. While wearing a mask, you can use an action to transform into a creature of the mask's type (fiend for Diabolica, fey for Fiabesco, celestial for Angelico, or humanoid for Umano) that you have seen before. The creature's Challenge Rating can be no higher than 1 (this increases to 3 at 6th level). Your transformation uses the creature's stat block with the following rules: Only your Intelligence score, memories, and alignment stay the same. All other statistics change to the creature's. If an ability in the creature's stat block refers to a DC, it uses your spell save DC instead. You retain your Bardic Inspiration feature but can't cast spells unless the creature's form can. You can't concentrate on spells you cast before transforming. You assume the creature's hit points and Hit Dice. When you revert, you return to the hit points you had before transforming. If the form drops to 0 hit points, excess damage carries over to your normal form. You choose whether your equipment falls to the ground, merges into the new form, or is worn by it. Equipment that merges has no effect until you revert. The transformation lasts for the remaining duration of the mask. When the form ends — whether by dropping to 0 hit points, the duration expiring, or you choosing to revert (no action required) — the mask's effect also ends and counts as a used mask for the day. Suggested Stat Blocks. Fiend: Imp, L'anima Vuota, Red Hand of Mammon, Il Rosso, Il Caduto Fey: Vivo, Arcobaleno, Sprite, Pixie Celestial: Fated One, Hidden One, Radiant One Humanoid: Thug, Commoner, Noble, Merman Crafting a Mask. If any of your masks are destroyed, you can spend 1 hour (which can overlap with a short rest) and use specific dye and wood in the process to create a new one. Lending the Mask: You can lend your mask to another willing humanoid. The humanoid must not have a negative Charisma modifier, and you must also expend a Bardic Inspiration die for that humanoid to be able to use the mask.

features.name: The Hidden Power
features.text: Your bond with your masks deepens, and their power grows. Your Assume Form maximum CR increases to 3. Inspired Masks. While wearing a mask, when you grant a creature a Bardic Inspiration die, that creature also gains temporary hit points equal to the number rolled.

features.name: Masked Potential Unleashed
features.text: Your masks have become extensions of your soul. Your mask duration extends to 1 hour. The Two-Faced. Once per Long Rest, as an action, you can don both of your masks simultaneously. For 1 minute, you can take the form of a creature of either mask's type. While in this state, your Masked Resilience temporary hit points are doubled.
